transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Valor Head of Platform), Marcus Lee (Valor Security), Amy Nguyen (Valor PM)

Summary: Quick product walkthrough focused on data retention and PII controls in Redwood Console and API. Demonstrated toggles for storing request/response payloads, automated PII redaction, and audit log visibility. Discussed encryption/KMS and private deployment tradeoffs for PCI scope.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for taking time today, i'm maya from redwood, arjun is our se and we'll run through how we handle data and retention controls in the console and the api. can you quick intro who you are?
00:12 Lena Ortiz: lena here, head of platform at valor payments. responsible for infra and compliance.
00:16 Marcus Lee: marcus, security engineer. i'll be primary on the PCI/scope questions.
00:20 Amy Nguyen: amy, product manager on the payments platform, interested in how we surface PII concerns to product.
00:26 Maya Chen: great. quick agenda: demo the console toggles for request storage, show automated pii redaction, logging redaction and audit logs, and then talk about kms, vpc, and dedicated options. we'll leave 10 minutes for q&a and next steps.
00:40 Arjun Patel: i'll share my screen, just a heads up transcription may pick up some of the UI names oddly. starting on the console home.
:00:52 Arjun Patel: so this is the route config page. first thing to note - per-route retention and storage toggles. you can set request storage to on/off at the route level, so if you have a payments route you can disable request storage entirely.
01:12 Lena Ortiz: when you say storage off, is that still logged anywhere? like are there any traces left for debugging?
01:18 Arjun Patel: good question. there are three layers: application-level request payload storage (what you toggle off), metadata logs (we keep minimal metadata for billing/tracing unless you opt out), and ephemeral request logs used for debugging which are zeroed out after the retention window. when storage is off for a route, payload content is not persisted. our audit logs will still show that a request was processed but not the full payload.
01:40 Marcus Lee: what's the retention window options? we need 30 days for certain teams, but for PCI stuff we may want 0 retention.
01:48 Arjun Patel: you can set a retention window at the org level and override per-route. options are 0 (no payload storage), 7, 30, 90, 365 days. also you can set redact-only mode where the payload is stored but PII fields are redacted.
02:05 Maya Chen: i'll jump in with an example. arjun, can you demo turning off storage for a route and show the logs?
02:12 Arjun Patel: sure. navigating to route "payments-checkout-prod" -> settings -> data controls. toggling request storage: off. now if i replay a sample request — note: this is a synthetic request — you'll see the request body will not appear in stored requests but you'll see a needle in the audit log that a request id was processed at timestamp.
02:34 Arjun Patel: (replay) -- ok, request created, audit entry shows request-id 8c4f..., payload not persisted.
02:42 Marcus Lee: can you show me the audit log entry format? is it possible to export that for SIEM?
02:47 Arjun Patel: yes, audit logs include request id, route, model variant, timestamp, status, and redaction status. i'll open the audit export, csv/json export options exist, and you can ship them to your cloud storage or SIEM via our connector.
03:07 Amy Nguyen: how about redaction rules — is it regex-based or ML-based? we're concerned about edge cases in card numbers and tokens.
03:14 Arjun Patel: we use a hybrid. default automatic PII detection is ML-first with heuristics for common patterns (credit cards, ssn, email, phone). for payments we recommend adding a custom redaction rule set — you can provide regex or a tokenization map. there's also a tester in the console to run sample payloads and see what gets redacted. i'll open the redaction tester.
03:38 Arjun Patel: (opens tester) paste a sample: {card_number: 4111 1111 1111 1111, cvv: 123}. tester output shows card_number -> [REDACTED-CARD], cvv -> [REDACTED-CVV], rest of text unchanged. note: tester logs are ephemeral unless you save the test; we mark those as debug/test logs.
03:58 Marcus Lee: does redaction happen client-side or server-side? we can't send unhashed card data outside of our network in some flows.
04:04 Arjun Patel: redaction is server-side in the redwood inference plane. however, for highest compliance needs, we offer private deployments or routing through your VPC where data never leaves your network. practically, that means you can run the inference plane in your VPC or on-prem and control ingress. this reduces PCI scope as card numbers never traverse public infrastructure.
04:26 Lena Ortiz: and kms/hsm — where do keys live?
04:30 Maya Chen: we support BYOK via customer-managed KMS. so encryption at rest of stored payloads is with your KMS keys. for hosted customers we provide an option to integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or an HSM partner. keys are not available to Redwood employees.
04:46 Marcus Lee: is there an attestable audit trail for key usage? we need to prove who rotated or used keys.
04:52 Arjun Patel: yes, key usage logs are surfaced in the audit logs and you can configure alerts on key rotations. For dedicated/private, you control rotation and we integrate with your KMS API.
05:04 Amy Nguyen: what about streaming responses? if we stream tokens back, does the streamed data flow through logs?
05:10 Arjun Patel: streaming is similar: if request storage is off, we don't persist the response tokens. you can also enable token-level redact rules, e.g., stop streaming if a sensitive pattern is detected.
05:25 Lena Ortiz: can you describe "redact-only mode" again?
05:28 Arjun Patel: redact-only means we store the payload but PII fields are replaced with placeholder tokens so you can still use the payload for usage analytics without PII. helpful for model quality monitoring.
05:40 Maya Chen: i'm going to demo the console flow for redact-only and then the api param.
05:44 Arjun Patel: api side, there's an optional header x-redwood-storage: off|redact-only|on. when set to off, payloads not stored. when redact-only, we persist redacted payloads. we also have a per-request param to pass a pii_schema or custom redaction map.
06:02 Marcus Lee: is the api header authenticated? could devs accidentally flip it?
06:06 Arjun Patel: it's part of the authenticated request, but anyone with api keys can set it. for governance we recommend RBAC with required approvals for production route changes. you can lock toggles behind org policies and SSO groups.
06:20 Maya Chen: quick look at RBAC - you can set route-level policies so only users in redwood role "data-admin" can change storage settings.
06:28 Amy Nguyen: we have a hybrid team, will your SSO integrate with our okta groups for policy enforcement?
06:32 Arjun Patel: yes, we support SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, and group mapping so you can map okta groups to roles.
06:40 Lena Ortiz: on the private deployment side, what's the effort? we have strict PCI segmentation and may need an on-prem instance.
06:46 Arjun Patel: private has two flavors: VPC-hosted (we deploy in your cloud account) and on-prem appliance. VPC-hosted is typically 2-4 weeks with infra templates; on-prem is a longer engagement with our infra team. both can be configured to never persist payloads outside your environment and integrate with your KMS.
07:08 Marcus Lee: do you offer guaranteed deletion? e.g., purge all historic payloads older than X?
07:12 Arjun Patel: yes, we have a purge API where you can programmatically delete stored payloads by route, by date range, or by request id. we also support org-level auto-purge policies.
07:24 Lena Ortiz: if we request deletion, is there a confirmation trace that we can show to auditors?
07:28 Arjun Patel: deletion events are recorded in the audit log with who initiated the purge and timestamp; you can export that.
07:34 Maya Chen: switching gears: show how this ties into Optimize and quality monitoring. arjun?
07:38 Arjun Patel: Optimize collects token-level telemetry and quality metrics. when storage is on or redact-only, Optimize can run rule-based evals against redacted payloads to detect regressions. you can configure evals using prompt sets and set alerts for quality regression.
07:54 Amy Nguyen: in redact-only mode, will the eval be meaningful if PII is replaced?
07:58 Arjun Patel: yes, because redaction replaces PII with consistent tokens, the semantic structure remains. for many evals that's enough. for sensitive evals requiring raw PII, you should run them in a private deployment or local test harness.
08:14 Marcus Lee: what about token-level cost visibility? we need to reconcile spend to requests without seeing payloads.
08:20 Arjun Patel: billing records include token counts per request id and route, not payload contents. you can export usage with request ids and timestamps and join that offline with your internal datasets if needed.
08:34 Maya Chen: quick question from sales ops: any competitor features you want highlighted?
08:38 Amy Nguyen: (customer) sorry, wrong person.
08:40 Lena Ortiz: do you have any comparative notes vs Anthropic or self-hosting?
08:44 Maya Chen: briefly: compared to Anthropic's managed endpoints, Redwood focuses on per-route controls and first-class private deployment options with RBAC/console controls; vs self-hosting, Redwood adds auto-batching, smart routing and observability out of the box.
09:00 Marcus Lee: ok can we dig into the redaction false positive/neg rate? we need numbers for the privacy team.
09:06 Arjun Patel: we have internal evals: baseline pii-detection recall ~96% on common PII classes, precision ~94% on our test sets. for payments-specific patterns we can tune with custom rules to reach >99% recall. we'll share the evaluation spreadsheet in the docs we send.
09:26 Lena Ortiz: when you say "we'll share" that's the security binder?
09:30 Maya Chen: yes i'll attach SOC 2, data flow diagrams, our redaction model evaluation spreadsheet, and KMS integration docs.
09:36 Amy Nguyen: for the POC, what's realistic scope? full sandbox of checkout flows?
09:40 Arjun Patel: typically we do a 1-week POC: provision a test route, enable redact-only and off modes, run your sample payloads through the API, and validate redaction and retention behaviors. we can include a small dedicated GPU pool if you want to test latency under load.
09:58 Marcus Lee: latency under token-redaction — is there a perf hit for redaction?
10:02 Arjun Patel: minimal. redaction runs before persistence, not in the inference path, so it doesn't add per-token latency to generation. redaction does add a small processing time for storage operations, but it's batched.
10:18 Amy Nguyen: any options to redact at the SDK layer before hitting redwood?
10:22 Arjun Patel: yes, we have client libraries with local pre-send hooks where you can run your own redaction/tokenization. for example, our node sdk exposes a preSend middleware.
10:34 Lena Ortiz: show the api call example for setting x-redwood-storage and a pii_schema param?
10:38 Arjun Patel: example: POST /v1/generate with header x-redwood-storage: redact-only and body {"prompt":"...","pii_schema":{"card_number":"card_regex","email":"email_regex"}}. response includes request_id and redaction_summary.
10:58 Marcus Lee: can redaction be applied retroactively to stored payloads? we have legacy logs to sanitize.
11:04 Arjun Patel: we support retrospective purge and a re-redact job that will reprocess stored payloads to replace newly-detected patterns, but note that re-redact requires the raw payload to be present or a legal hold if you need to preserve the original.
11:22 Maya Chen: we've covered most tabletop items; remaining questions?
11:26 Lena Ortiz: two risks: 1) developers accidentally enabling storage, 2) audit trail completeness. how do you propose mitigating #1?
11:33 Arjun Patel: mitigation: enforce org policies so only infra admins can change route toggles, require change approvals in the console, and alert on any toggle changes via webhook to your SIEM.
11:44 Marcus Lee: #2 looks fine with audit exports and purge confirmation logs. can you also send a sample export format so our compliance team can review?
11:50 Maya Chen: yes will include sample audit export.
11:54 Amy Nguyen: last operational question: if a request identifies a sensitive token mid-stream, can we auto-abort?
11:59 Arjun Patel: yes, you can configure a server-side filter to abort or redact and stop streaming. we expose webhooks for intercepts too.
12:10 Maya Chen: wrapping up — proposed next steps: we'll send security binder and pricing, provision keys for POC, and schedule a kickoff next tuesday.
12:20 Lena Ortiz: thanks, that works. we'll prepare sample payloads and acceptance criteria.
12:25 Marcus Lee: i'll gather our PCI requirements and share them.
12:30 Maya Chen: awesome. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with docs and the POC plan.
